political.name: Revise the Racial Settlement
political.reduce: Relax Racial Classification and Pass Controls
political.restore: Reinstate Racial Classification and Pass Controls
political.desc: The franchise, racial classification and restrictions on residence sustain minority rule. A negotiated revision can reduce the burden of policing and separate administration, but it also gives up institutions on which the governing settlement depends.

services.name: Broaden Access to Public Services
services.reduce: Extend Equal Access to Public Services
services.desc: Public hospitals, schools and welfare provision are divided by race and funded unequally. Extending equal access raises the cost of provision while reducing the exceptional spending expectations associated with a privileged minority.

labour.name: Negotiate Labour and Land Reform
labour.restore: Restore Protected Labour and Land Arrangements
labour.desc: Restricted bargaining rights and access to land favour established employers and commercial farms. Opening employment and land institutions reduces these advantages, while easing the staffing difficulties created by occupational exclusion.

military.name: Revise Military Service and Pay
military.reduce: Broaden Recruitment and Standardise Military Pay
military.restore: Restore Preferential Military Service and Pay
military.desc: A narrow pool of eligible skilled recruits and the political importance of the armed services sustain privileged personnel arrangements. Wider recruitment and a common pay structure can reduce their cost and the exceptional defence-spending demands of minority rule.

population.name: Reconsider Settlement and Family Policy
population.reduce: Expand Voluntary Family Planning and Revise Settlement Incentives
population.restore: Restore Settlement Incentives and Previous Family Policy
population.desc: Selective settlement incentives coexist with contract migration and rapid natural growth in a youthful population. Voluntary family-planning provision and revised migration incentives can gradually change these pressures. Such trends arise from social conditions and population structure, rather than racial characteristics.
